title: Count the Number of Consistent Strings
description:
# Count the Number of Consistent Strings

You are given a string `allowed` consisting of distinct lowercase English letters and an array of strings `words`.

A word is consistent if every character in that word appears in `allowed`. Return the number of consistent strings in `words`.

## Example 1

**Input**
allowed = "ab", words = ["ad","bd","aaab","baa","badab"]

**Output**
2

**Explanation**
Only `"aaab"` and `"baa"` use characters from `allowed` exclusively.

## Example 2

**Input**
allowed = "abc", words = ["a","b","c","ab","ac","bc","abc"]

**Output**
7

**Explanation**
Every word uses only the letters `a`, `b`, and `c`.

## Example 3

**Input**
allowed = "cad", words = ["cc","acd","b","ba","bac","bad","ac","d"]

**Output**
4

**Explanation**
The consistent words are `"cc"`, `"acd"`, `"ac"`, and `"d"`.

## Constraints

* `1 <= words.length <= 10000`
* `1 <= allowed.length <= 26`
* `1 <= words[i].length <= 10`
* The characters in `allowed` are distinct.
* `words[i]` and `allowed` contain only lowercase English letters.

solutions.name: Boolean Allowed Set
solutions.description:
## Approach
Create a boolean table of length `26`, where `allowedTable[c - 'a']` tells whether a lowercase letter is allowed. Then scan each word and reject it as soon as one character is not marked.

## Key Insight
The alphabet size is fixed. Repeated allowed letters inside a word are fine; the only thing that matters is whether every character belongs to the allowed set.

## Complexity Analysis
Let `A` be `allowed.length()` and `L` be the total number of characters across `words`. Building the table costs O(A), scanning the words costs O(L), so the total time complexity is O(A + L). The table always has 26 slots, so the extra space complexity is O(1).

solutions.name: Bitmask Subset Check
solutions.description:
## Approach
Encode `allowed` as a 26-bit integer mask. For each word, build its own mask and count it only when the word mask has no bit outside the allowed mask.

## Key Insight
A word is consistent exactly when its set of letters is a subset of the allowed set. The expression `(wordMask & ~allowedMask) == 0` is that subset test written as bit operations.

## Complexity Analysis
Building masks reads each relevant character once, so the time complexity is O(A + L). Two integer masks are used regardless of input size, so the space complexity is O(1).

solutions.name: HashSet Allowed Characters
solutions.description:
## Approach
Insert every character from `allowed` into a `HashSet<Character>`. For each word, check every character with set membership and count the word only if all checks pass.

## Key Insight
This is the most general set-model solution: build a membership set first, then ask whether each word contains only members of that set. Under this problem's lowercase alphabet, the set size is bounded by 26.

## Complexity Analysis
The algorithm inserts `A` allowed characters and scans `L` word characters, so the time complexity is O(A + L). The set contains at most 26 lowercase letters, so the extra space complexity is O(1).
